exposure: Type of immediate breast reconstruction (Latissimus Dorsi flap, Transverse Rectus Abdominis Myocutaneous flap)
cohort: 45 patients undergoing immediate breast reconstruction for operable breast tumors, excluding those with recurrent, bilateral, metastatic, or locally advanced disease.
finding: The Latissimus Dorsi (LD) flap technique was associated with potential benefits in post-operative recovery and complication management, including a lower incidence of significant seroma, compared to the Transverse Rectus Abdominis Myocutaneous (TRAM) flap procedure, which had longer hospital stays, surgery duration, and higher rates of donor site infection and deformity.
